userReferenceImages.observed: Retro train platform: fine structural joints, restrained grey-green concrete and paint, cornered local abrasions; broad quiet material fields retain their own colour.
Retro low-poly laboratory: separate grey-green metal, stone-grey floor and warm wood; deliberate hard-edged adjacent pixel clusters express chipped paint and exposed underlayers.

photoGrounding: Retain the original rooftop photographs as evidence for connected fissures, local mortar repair, scrubbed joints, aggregate and shallow weathering; interpret those material features with the new supplied pixel-cluster reference style.
paintDecisions: Remove the previous broad rounded pale floor blobs. New local defects are roughly 3–11 source pixels across, with square steps and chipped corners.
Keep readable thin structural slab joints as displaced interrupted 1 px fragments. Do not create a repeated complete tile grid or aligned long bars.
Crack networks branch at explicitly placed sites, with local mortar fill, small pore clusters and a few warm old-mortar cores under flaking grey cement.
Plaster has its own grey-green pigment; selected chips expose warmer plaster. Damp is confined to unequal short sites and fissures, rather than a uniform bottom stripe.
Cap stone uses a paler mineral palette, cement a cooler middle grey-green, and iron a visibly different grey-blue with a small number of edge/joint rust chips and short runs.
Preserve all brick-red roof painting and previously cleared Chinese shop signs unchanged. No geometry, UV, camera, runtime or atmosphere file was edited by this painting task.
referenceUse: The two supplied images were viewed and studied. No image pixels were traced, copied, downscaled into a texture or generated. Pixelorama performed every painted atlas pixel through its actual native Pencil.
